golem.role: The Golem (Kiro) — starts confused, becomes confident

segments.text: Tuesday morning. You arrive at the Builders' Guild. The hallway is empty.
The previous architect — Marcus — quit last Friday. No handoff. No notes. Just a half-built project and a client demo tomorrow.
On your desk: a dormant golem, a stack of scattered documents, and a blinking message.
This is Lord Ashford. My social platform launches tomorrow. I was told the new architect would handle it. Don't disappoint me.
The golem's eyes flicker. It tries to speak.
I... I don't know what I am. I have no context. No instructions. Tell me what to do.
A young apprentice bursts through the door. Oh! You're the new architect! I'm Pip! The golem needs specs to build anything — without them it just... makes stuff up.
The clock on the wall reads 9:00 AM. The demo is at 9:40. Your forty minutes start now.
Ashford here. Twenty minutes left. Tell me you have something to show.
The message light blinks red. Pip looks at you nervously.
We're halfway there! The golem is building but... we still need to test and deploy.
The golem hums steadily. It's working. But the clock doesn't care.
The deployment completes. The URL goes live. You paste it into the message.
All systems nominal. Build complete. Tests passing. Deployed to production.
Long pause. ...It works. It actually works. On your first day. I'm impressed.
We did it! Spec-driven development for the win!
You lean back. The golem's eyes glow steady blue. It knows what it is now.
And tomorrow, when the next project comes, you'll both be ready.
Time's up. I'm looking at a blank page. We'll talk Monday.
The demo slot passes. Lord Ashford disconnects. Pip slumps in his chair.
I was close. I understand the architecture now. Next time will be different.
Tomorrow, you'll be faster. The specs are written. The golem remembers.
Next time, you'll ship.
